doc.title: Germaine Bazzle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 21, 2006

title: The fine arts department at her private school
summary: Music, drama and art teachers work together so students learn phrasing and expression from each other.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Do students in — are you in a public school?
No, I’m in a private school.
In a private school, they have a lot of musical opportunities in that private school?

Um hum. Yes. And you know we have I think a pretty good fine arts department. We have piano and instrumental music and vocal music and drama and art and all of that kind of thing. And those of us who are in that department, we actually — we work together so that our kids are benefiting from all of the areas, so that a person who is sitting down watching the speaker, the person who is a singer sitting down watching the speaker has something to go by, to listen to. Notice things. You know, notice the phrasing, notice the enunciation, notice these kinds of things so that you as a singer must understand that that’s part of singing, enunciation, phrasing. That’s part of it too. Expression. Showing it on your face. That’s part of it too. So look at the actor and then project that through your singing. And then it’s the same thing. The actor looks at the singer and notices well what’s happening here with the dynamics, what are we doing? It works.
Yeah. There’s something to learn from every art form.
